prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1482; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection and a right knee injury from striking the dash. The insured driver is named on the policy, and the claim was opened the same day.

Entry 2: Police confirmed the claimant was a passenger in the vehicle at the scene, and two responding officers recorded the same location. No independent witnesses to the impact have come forward, and no photos of the scene were submitted.

Entry 3: Repair estimate shows rear bumper and trunk lid damage consistent with the described impact. No prior damage to the vehicle appears in our records or in the inspection notes.

Entry 4: Claimant's knee injury is a plausible result of a collision of this type, and the initial medical report describes a bruised and swollen knee. No prior injury to the same knee appears in the claimant's history.

Entry 5: Claimant has given the same account of the collision in each call so far, with no changes to the sequence or location. A neighbor contacted our office and said the car looked damaged several weeks before the reported date, though the neighbor did not witness any collision.

Entry 6: Treatment has grown to many times the typical amount for this injury, with visits nearly every day over the past several weeks. New complaints involving the shoulder and lower back were added weeks after the collision, and the claimant has not provided an explanation for the timing.

Entry 7: Claim is being held for further review of the treatment records and the neighbor's statement. Claimant has not retained an attorney, and I have sent a written request for the complete medical file and prior vehicle service history.
